questions.question: Two numbers are 30% and 20% less than a third number respectively. The ratio of first two numbers is:
questions.solution:
**Given:**

First number = 30% less than the third number.

Second number = 20% less than the third number.

**Formula used:**

Percentage decrease: {New value} = {Original value} times (1 - frac{{Percentage decrease}}{100}) 

Ratio of the two numbers = frac{{First number}}{{Second number}}

**Calculations:**

Let the third number = 100.

First number = 100 times (1 - (30)/(100)) = 100 times 0.7 = 70 

Second number = 100 times (1 - (20)/(100)) = 100 times 0.8 = 80 

Ratio of first number to second number:

(70)/(80) = (7)/(8)

**∴ The ratio of the first two numbers is 7:8.**

questions.question: The aim of Swachh Bharat Mission (Gramin) was to achieve a clean and Open Defecation Free (ODF) India by:

• The Swachh Bharat Mission (Gramin) was launched on 2nd October 2014 by Prime Minister Narendra Modi.

• Key components included solid waste management, construction of individual household latrines, and public awareness campaigns.
 
• Municipalities were given targets to achieve ODF status and improve waste management systems.
 
 
 
• **Open Defecation Free (ODF) Status**
 
 
• ODF status is achieved when no one in a community defecates in the open, and all households have access to functional toilets.
 
• ODF verification involves multiple levels of assessment to ensure sustainable toilet usage and maintenance.
 
• Villages achieving ODF status contribute to improving public health and environmental conditions.

• Public participation was encouraged through awareness campaigns, community-led initiatives, and involvement of local leaders.
 
• The mission aimed to create a sense of ownership and responsibility towards maintaining cleanliness among citizens.

questions.question: Lactic acid is mainly found in:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Curd**__.

__
 
• Lactic acid is produced by the bacterial fermentation of lactose found in milk.
 
• Curd is a dairy product obtained by coagulating milk in a process called curdling.
 
• The bacteria used to make curd are known as lactic acid bacteria (LAB), which convert lactose into lactic acid.
 
• Lactic acid gives curd its characteristic tangy taste and thick texture.
 
• Consumption of curd provides beneficial probiotics that aid in digestion and improve gut health.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• Fermentation is a metabolic process that produces chemical changes in organic substrates through the action of enzymes.
 
• In the context of dairy products, it specifically refers to the conversion of sugars into acids, gases, or alcohol.
 
• Lactic acid fermentation is used in the production of foods like yogurt, cheese, and sourdough bread.
 
 
 
• **Lactic Acid Bacteria (LAB)**
 
 
• LAB are a group of Gram-positive bacteria that produce lactic acid as the major metabolic end product of carbohydrate fermentation.
 
• These bacteria are commonly found in decomposing plants and milk products.
 
• They are used in the food industry for fermentation and as probiotics.
 
 
 
• **Probiotics**
 
 
• Probiotics are live microorganisms that provide health benefits when consumed in adequate amounts.
 
• They help maintain a healthy balance of gut bacteria and can improve digestive health.
 
• Common probiotic foods include yogurt, kefir, sauerkraut, and curd.
 
 
 
• **Nutritional Benefits of Curd**
 
 
• Curd is rich in protein, calcium, vitamin B12, and riboflavin.
 
• It can help improve digestion, boost the immune system, and promote bone health.
 
• Regular consumption of curd is associated with various health benefits, including improved gut health and reduced risk of heart disease.

questions.question: Who was the first Governor General of Bengal ?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Warren Hastings**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Warren Hastings served as the first Governor-General of Bengal from 1773 to 1785.
 
• He was appointed under the Regulating Act of 1773, which was the first step towards central administration in India.
 
• Hastings played a crucial role in the consolidation of British power in India during the early years of colonial rule.
 
• His tenure was marked by administrative reforms, including the reorganization of revenue collection and the judicial system.
 
• Warren Hastings' governance laid the foundation for subsequent British policies in India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Regulating Act of 1773:**

 
 
• This was the first act passed by the British Parliament to regulate the affairs of the East India Company in India.
 
• It marked the beginning of parliamentary control over the Company's administration in India.
 
• The Act established the position of Governor-General of Bengal along with an Executive Council of four members to assist him.
 
 
 
• **Administrative Reforms:**
 
 
• Hastings introduced judicial reforms, including the establishment of civil and criminal courts.
 
• He aimed to standardize revenue collection procedures and reduce corruption.
 
• His efforts were directed towards creating a more efficient and centralized administrative framework.
 
 
 
• **Anglo-Mysore Wars:**
 
 
• During Hastings' tenure, the First and Second Anglo-Mysore Wars were fought between the British East India Company and the Kingdom of Mysore.
 
• These conflicts were significant in expanding British influence in southern India.
 
 
 
• **Legacy:**
 
 
• Hastings' policies and administrative measures set the groundwork for future British governance in India.
 
• Despite controversies and impeachment trials in Britain, his contributions to the establishment of British rule are acknowledged by historians.

questions.question: The term pisciculture is related with:
questions.solution:

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Pisciculture refers to the breeding, rearing, and transplantation of fish by artificial means.
 
• It is a branch of aquaculture, specifically focusing on the cultivation of fish in controlled environments.
 
• This practice is used to increase fish production for commercial purposes.
 
• Common species cultivated through pisciculture include carp, catfish, tilapia, and salmon.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• **Mariculture**
 
 
• Mariculture is a specialized branch of aquaculture involving the cultivation of marine organisms in the open ocean or in enclosed sections of the ocean.
 
• It includes the farming of species such as oysters, clams, mussels, and seaweed.
 
 
 
• **Inland Fisheries**
 
 
• Inland fisheries focus on the cultivation and harvesting of fish in freshwater environments like rivers, lakes, and ponds.
 
• This practice is vital for enhancing fish production in non-coastal areas.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a metal?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Phosphorus**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Phosphorus is a non-metal.**
 
• It is a chemical element with the symbol **P** and atomic number 15.
 
• Phosphorus exists in several forms, the most common being white and red phosphorus.
 
• It is essential for life, playing a key role in the formation of DNA, RNA, and ATP.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Metals vs Non-metals:**

 
 
• Metals are typically malleable, ductile, and good conductors of heat and electricity.
 
• Non-metals, on the other hand, are usually brittle (if solid), and poor conductors of heat and electricity.
 
• Examples of metals include Aluminium, Mercury, and Sodium.
 
• Examples of non-metals include Phosphorus, Carbon, and Sulfur.
 
 
 
• **Types of Phosphorus:**
 
 
• **White Phosphorus:** Highly reactive and is used in military applications like incendiary bombs.
 
• **Red Phosphorus:** More stable and used in safety matches, fireworks, and pesticides.
 
 
 
• **Phosphorus in Biology:**
 
 
• Phosphorus is a key component of DNA and RNA, which are essential for genetic information transfer.
 
• It is also vital in the formation of ATP (adenosine triphosphate), the energy currency of cells.
 
• Phosphates are an important part of bones and teeth in the form of calcium phosphate.
 
 
 
• **Environmental Impact:**
 
 
• Excess phosphorus in water bodies can lead to eutrophication, causing algal blooms that deplete oxygen and harm aquatic life.
 
• Managing phosphorus levels in agriculture and waste management is crucial to prevent environmental degradation.

questions.question: How many members are nominated in the Rajya Sabha by the President of India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**12**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The President of India can nominate up to **12 members** to the Rajya Sabha.
 
• These nominations are made under **Article 80** of the Indian Constitution.
 
• The nominated members are chosen for their expertise in fields such as literature, science, art, and social service.
 
• This provision ensures that the Rajya Sabha has representation from distinguished individuals who have made significant contributions to society.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Article 80 of the Indian Constitution:**

 
 
• This article deals with the composition of the Rajya Sabha.
 
• It specifies the maximum strength of the Rajya Sabha as 250 members.
 
• Out of these, 238 members are representatives of the States and Union Territories, and 12 are nominated by the President.
 
 
 
• **Role of Rajya Sabha:**
 
 
• The Rajya Sabha is the Upper House of the Parliament of India.
 
• It represents the States and Union Territories of India.
 
• Members of the Rajya Sabha review, amend, and pass legislation.
 
• It acts as a permanent house and is not subject to dissolution.
 
 
 
• **Eligibility for Nomination:**
 
 
• Nominated members are chosen for their expertise and contributions to society.
 
• They are not required to have any political affiliation.
 
• This ensures a non-partisan representation of eminent personalities in the Rajya Sabha.
 
 
 
• **Notable Nominated Members:**
 
 
• Some notable nominated members include Lata Mangeshkar (singer), Sachin Tendulkar (cricketer), and Raghuram Rajan (economist).
 
• These members have brought their expertise and perspective to legislative discussions.

questions.question: The dance form Kuchipudi originated in:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Andhra Pradesh**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Kuchipudi is a classical Indian dance form that originated in the state of **Andhra Pradesh**.
 
• The dance form is named after the village of **Kuchipudi** in the Krishna district of Andhra Pradesh.
 
• Kuchipudi is known for its graceful movements and strong narrative/dramatic character.
 
• This dance form incorporates both **nritta (pure dance)** and **nritya (expressive dance)** elements.
 
• The dance traditionally tells stories from Hindu epics and mythology, especially those of Lord Krishna.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Terminology in Kuchipudi:**

 
 
• **Natya:** The dramatic element of dance, including the spoken word.
 
• **Nritta:** The pure dance movements performed rhythmically without any interpretative aspect.
 
• **Nritya:** The expressive aspect of dance that conveys a narrative or emotions.
 
• **Abhinaya:** The art of expression in Indian classical dance.
 
 
 
• **Historical Context:**
 
 
• Kuchipudi dance form was originally performed by male Brahmins known as **Bhagavathalu**.
 
• It evolved into a more inclusive art form over time, now performed by both men and women.
 
 
 
• **Famous Practitioners:**
 
 
• Some renowned Kuchipudi dancers include **Yamini Krishnamurthy** and **Sobha Naidu**.
 
• These artists have significantly contributed to the propagation and modernization of Kuchipudi.
 
 
 
• **Costume and Music:**
 
 
• Kuchipudi dancers wear traditional attire, which includes a saree for women and a dhoti for men, often adorned with jewelry.
 
• The music accompanying Kuchipudi is typically Carnatic, and performances often feature live musicians.

questions.question: kilowatt hour (kW.h) is a unit of:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**energy**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• A kilowatt hour (kW.h) is a unit of **energy**.
 
• It is commonly used to measure electrical energy consumption.
 
• One kilowatt hour is equivalent to the energy consumption of a 1000-watt appliance running for one hour.
 
• The kilowatt hour is a derived unit of energy in the International System of Units (SI).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Energy:** The capacity to do work, measured in joules (J) in the SI system, but kilowatt hours (kW.h) are used for practical electrical energy measurement.
 
• **Power:** The rate at which energy is used or transferred, measured in watts (W). 1 watt = 1 joule per second.
 
• **Joule:** The SI unit of energy, defined as the energy transferred when applying a force of one newton over a distance of one meter.
 
• **Electricity Billing:** Household electricity bills typically use kilowatt hours to quantify energy consumption.
 
• **Conversion:** 1 kilowatt hour = 3.6 million joules (3.6 x 10⁶ J).

questions.question: Who is the Chief Election Commissioner of India as of November 2020?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Sunil Arora**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Sunil Arora served as the Chief Election Commissioner of India from **December 2, 2018, to April 12, 2021**.
 
• He succeeded Om Prakash Rawat and was succeeded by Sushil Chandra.
 
• During his tenure, Sunil Arora oversaw the 2019 General Elections in India, one of the largest democratic exercises in the world.
 
• Arora had a distinguished career in the Indian Administrative Service (IAS) before his appointment as the Chief Election Commissioner.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Election Commission of India (ECI)**

 
 
• The ECI is an autonomous constitutional authority responsible for administering election processes in India at both the national and state levels.
 
• It was established on January 25, 1950, to ensure free and fair elections in the country.
 
• The commission is composed of a Chief Election Commissioner and two Election Commissioners.
 
• ECI’s major functions include the preparation of electoral rolls, supervision of elections, and ensuring the implementation of the model code of conduct.
 
 
 
• **Role of Chief Election Commissioner (CEC)**
 
 
• The CEC is the head of the Election Commission of India and is responsible for ensuring elections are conducted impartially and fairly.
 
• The CEC is appointed by the President of India and usually has a tenure of six years or up to the age of 65, whichever is earlier.
 
• The CEC can only be removed from office in a manner similar to the removal of a Supreme Court judge, that is through a process of impeachment by Parliament.

For the polynomial x2 - 9x + 18, we need to find factors of 18 that add up to -9.

Numbers are -3 and -6.

The factors of the polynomial x2 - 9x + 18 are (x - 3) and (x - 6).

• Vitamin D helps the body absorb calcium, which is essential for maintaining strong bones and teeth.

• Calcium deficiency can lead to osteoporosis, a condition characterized by weak and fragile bones.
 
 
 
• **Vitamin D Deficiency:**
 
 
• Vitamin D deficiency is common and can result in bone pain and muscle weakness.
 
• Risk factors for deficiency include limited sun exposure, darker skin, obesity, and certain medical conditions.
 
• Supplementation can help individuals who do not get enough Vitamin D from sunlight or their diet.
 
• Regular blood tests can help monitor Vitamin D levels in the body.

• During winter or in regions with low sunlight, dietary sources and supplements become more important.
 
 
 
• **Fortified Foods:**
 
 
• Many foods are fortified with Vitamin D to help prevent deficiencies, including milk, orange juice, and cereals.
 
• These fortified foods provide an additional source of Vitamin D, especially in individuals with limited sun exposure.
 
• Reading food labels can help identify fortified products and ensure adequate Vitamin D intake.
 
• Fortification has been a public health strategy to combat Vitamin D deficiency worldwide.

• The Central Processing Unit (CPU) is often referred to as the **brain of the computer** because it handles all instructions it receives from hardware and software running on the computer.
 
• CPUs perform the basic **arithmetic, logic, controlling, and input/output (I/O) operations** specified by the instructions in the program.
 
• The CPU consists of two main components: the **Arithmetic Logic Unit (ALU)**, which performs arithmetic and logical operations, and the **Control Unit (CU)**, which directs all processor operations.
 
• Modern CPUs are typically made up of multiple cores, which allow for **parallel processing** and can significantly increase computing power.
 
• The speed of a CPU is measured in **GHz (gigahertz)**, which indicates how many cycles per second it can execute.

• **Multi-core Processor**
 
 
• A multi-core processor is a single computing component with two or more independent CPUs (called "cores").
 
• Each core can run its own thread of instructions, improving overall performance and efficiency.
 
 
 
• **Hyper-threading**
 
 
• Hyper-threading is a technology used to improve parallelization of computations (doing multiple tasks at once).
 
• Introduced by Intel, it allows a single core to serve multiple threads.

• The clock speed of a CPU is the rate at which it can complete cycles, usually measured in GHz.
 
• Higher clock speeds generally mean faster performance, but other factors like core count and architecture also play significant roles.
